This sheet is a plain-language summary made with the help of AI from these sources. It does not replace them: read them to expand or check the information.

Each disorder sheet lists at the end the specific sources that were consulted, with links, and highlights the main one under “What it is”. They are official sources or reference organisations (WHO, Canal Salut, NHS, NICE, NIMH, MedlinePlus and others). The sheet is a summary: it may contain errors or become out of date, and it should be checked against these sources.

The usual treatments are psychological therapies, above all cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT). In some cases hypnotherapy or medication (antidepressants, beta blockers or sedatives) may also be considered, always at the discretion of a professional.

Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the first-choice treatment according to the European and North American clinical guidelines. Sleep hygiene measures help: regular schedules, avoiding screens, caffeine and alcohol before bed, and a dark, quiet room at a comfortable temperature. Sleeping pills are only considered for short periods and under medical supervision.

According to a survey of experts by the ISTSS, most recommend a phased approach: first safety and stabilisation (emotional regulation, calming skills), then processing of the trauma with trauma-focused therapies (trauma-focused CBT, EMDR) and, finally, reintegration into daily life. Not all professionals agree, and the pace is set by the person.
